name: Sierra de Tramuntana (Ma-10)
description: Mallorca's mountain road from Andratx to Pollença past Deià and Valldemossa, with the hairpins down to Sa Calobra

name: Sa Calobra
description: The 'snake': a road that loops under itself and coils down to a cove in the Tramuntana

name: Picos de Europa
description: Limestone peaks a short drive from the sea: the Desfiladero de La Hermida, Fuente Dé and the lakes of Covadonga

name: Desfiladero de La Hermida
description: A deep, narrow gorge into the Liébana valley, the gateway to the eastern Picos

name: White Towns of Andalusia
description: Ronda, Grazalema, Zahara and Arcos de la Frontera on hilltops over the Sierra de Grazalema

name: Sierra Nevada
description: From Granada up into Spain's highest mountains, and the Alpujarras' white villages on the southern slopes

name: Alpujarras
description: Terraced valleys and Berber-style villages (Pampaneira, Bubión, Capileira, Trevélez) on the Sierra Nevada's south side

name: Costa Brava
description: Rocky coves and fishing towns from Tossa de Mar to Cadaqués and Cap de Creus

name: Ordesa and the Pyrenees
wiki: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park
description: Through the Aragonese Pyrenees to Torla and the Ordesa canyon, with high passes nearby

name: Port de la Bonaigua
description: A 2,072 m Pyrenean pass between the Val d'Aran and the Pallars, with long sweeping bends

name: Cabo de Gata
description: Europe's driest coast: volcanic headlands, empty beaches and the lighthouse road near Almería

name: Rías Baixas
description: The Galician estuaries south of Santiago: seafood towns, vineyards and the coast road to Baiona

name: Teide (Tenerife)
description: Up through pine forest into the caldera around Spain's highest peak, a lunar landscape at 2,000 m
